title: GRASP: Expert, Creator, Controller
idea: GRASP is a set of rules for deciding which class gets a responsibility; Expert, Creator and Controller answer the three most common placement questions.
points: Information Expert: give a job to the class that holds the data it needs.
Creator: let B create A when B contains, records or closely uses A.
Controller: one non-UI object receives each system operation and delegates the real work.
In interviews, say which principle placed each method; it shows deliberate design.

messages.label: addTrack("Intro", 185)
messages.note: Controller: the UI hands the system operation to one object and knows nothing more.

messages.label: add(title, seconds)
messages.note: The controller delegates. It holds no rules about tracks or totals.

messages.label: new Track(...)
messages.note: Creator: `Playlist` contains tracks, so it creates them. Nobody else calls `new Track`.

messages.label: length()
messages.note: A second system operation arrives through the same controller from any screen.

messages.label: totalSeconds()
messages.note: Information Expert: `Playlist` holds the tracks, so it computes their total.

messages.label: seconds()
messages.note: Each `Track` reports its own length; the playlist only sums.

messages.label: "m:ss"
messages.note: Every screen gets the same answer because one class computes it.

code.title: The problem
code.caption: Screens create tracks and compute totals themselves. Two screens, two different answers.

walk.text: `Playlist` holds the data but has no behaviour. Others must reach in to use it.
Each screen calls `new Track` itself. Creation logic is copied, not owned.
The web screen sums seconds, then formats minutes and seconds.
The mobile screen divides each track first and loses the leftover seconds.
Compare the two lines: same playlist, two lengths. Duplicated logic drifts apart.

code.title: The fix
code.caption: Expert and Creator move behaviour into `Playlist`; a controller is the single entry point.

walk.text: `Track` rejects bad input, so an invalid track can never exist.
Creator: `Playlist` makes each `Track` because it contains them.
Expert: the class that holds the tracks computes their total.
Controller: receives system operations, gets its playlist by injection, and delegates.
Formatting lives once here, so every screen matches. Formatting is presentation, not a domain rule.
Both screens now agree, and the bad track is rejected at the domain boundary.

pitfalls: A controller that computes totals or rules itself becomes a god class; delegate domain work.
Putting logic in UI handlers duplicates it per screen; totals then disagree between web and mobile.
Expert applied blindly can drag database or UI code into domain classes; split those out.

quiz.q: A `Library` holds `Loan` objects. Which class should compute a member's total overdue fine?
options: The UI screen that shows the fine
A new FineUtils class with static helpers
The LibraryController, since it receives the request
Library, which holds the loans the fine needs
quiz.why: Information Expert: `Library` holds the loans and their due dates. The controller should only forward the request, and a static utility separates data from behaviour.

takeaway: Put each job where the data lives; route system operations through a controller.

starters: How is a GRASP controller different from an MVC controller?
When does Creator conflict with using a factory?
What if the data a job needs is spread over several classes?
